text:
maria: Heads up — started seeing a bunch of tiny-gpu pods in Pending and a spike in preempt evictions after the nodepool rolling upgrade in eu-west1b.
devon: saw that too, looks like the new image changed the node label for gpu-family which messed up our scheduler scores.
lei: any concrete logs? I only see eviction events and a few FailedPreemption messages.
maria: paste of recent events:
```
Warning  FailedScheduling  2m (x47 over 10m)  default-scheduler  0/24 nodes are available: 24 InsufficientGPU.
Normal   Preempted        2m (x12 over 8m)   kubelet            Preempted lower-priority pod "train-small-abc"
Warning  FailedPreemption 1m                 kube-scheduler     failed to find preemption victims: score mismatch
```
sam: ah — the new nodes have taint `gpu.family=rtx:NoSchedule` but our old tolerations rely on `gpu.arch` label. scheduler scoring plugin is returning -INF for some mixes so preemption search aborts.
devon: that would explain the chain: pods pending -> preempt attempt fails -> scheduler gives up -> user retries -> bursty spike. Anyone changed the tainting during the upgrade job?
lei: upgrade job annotated nodes with a rolling taint to drain, but a post-hook forgot to reconcile labels. ops-bot shows the commit: `infra/auto-upgrade: add node-label gpu.family` but not the toleration mapping.
maria: mitigation ideas:
- roll back node label change on a subset (canary) to stop the bad scoring
- temporarily widen preemption scoring search with `--min-similarity=0.1` (experimental)
- add a tolerant fallback scheduler policy that allows cross-family packing for tiny pods
sam: short-term: I'm pushing a daemonset that adds a legacy label `gpu.arch` to new nodes so existing tolerations match. That should reduce preempt churn in ~5 mins.
devon: +1 also provisioning cadence — we should drain and cordon more conservatively during node upgrades to avoid mass label drift.
lei: long-term: update the scheduler scoring plugin to treat missing family labels as compatible for pods with `requests.gpu <= 0.5` and add a migration plan for tolerations.
maria: tracking: created a brief runbook for this incident, linking infra PR and rollout: https://git.internal/r/infra/patch/2345
ops-bot: Incident created: #INC-2026 gpu-preempt-chain-eu-west1b — responders: @devon @maria
sam: temporary DS applied, will monitor CPU/GPU allocation and evictions for next 15m :eyes:
maria: thanks team — please post update in 10m, if evictions stop we can follow with a controlled relabel and smaller canary upgrade.
